subject: Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity for Percepta Health — isolation, scaling, SLA
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@perceptahealth.com>
Cc: T.J. Collins <tj.collins@perceptahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity for Percepta Health — isolation, scaling, SLA

Hi Lisa / T.J.,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so everyone has a single source of truth and clear next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: inference cost spikes and unpredictable latency during nightly batch scoring and daytime spikes for clinical-assist workflows.
- Regulatory requirement: datasets for model scoring must be logically isolated from other customers (need tenancy isolation and audit logs).
- Goal: predictable per-token/unit cost, sub-150ms tail latency for the short-text clinical-assist path, and a 99.9% availability SLA for production.

Current environment & workload notes you shared
- Nightly scoring: 1.2M docs over a 4h window, avg sequence length ~320 tokens.
- Real-time clinical-assist: peak 350 concurrent requests, p95 seq len ~64.
- Migrations: plan to onboard in two phases: scoring (Phase 1) then low-latency assist (Phase 2).

Suggested Redwood Dedicated approach
- Reserved pool: start with a 4-GPU reserved pool (A100 equivalent) with burst capacity to 6 GPUs for daytime spikes.
- Isolation: dedicated tenant + network isolation (VPC peering), per-request audit logging and KMS-managed keys per customer.
- Autoscaling & fallback: quick autoscale triggers for prefix caching on scoring jobs; recommended fallback to slightly smaller quantized model for extreme contention.
- SLA targets: propose initial commitment with a 99.9% uptime SLA and 150ms p95 latency target for the clinical-assist route; we'll validate in staging PoC.

Data / security checklist items we discussed (attached): SOC2 evidence, encryption at rest, retention window controls.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Percepta to confirm traffic shaping windows and priority of the two phases (reply by Wed EOD).
2) I’ll share a filled capacity workbook (attached) and an architecture diagram — please annotate and return with any mismatches.
3) Schedule a technical PoC week (we suggested 2 weeks) — options: Jun 29 or Jul 6.
4) Procurement start: we’ll provide a draft reserved-capacity term sheet after mutual alignment on sizing.

Attachments: percepta_capacity_workbook.xlsx (workbook for your traffic shapes), redwood-architecture-diagram.pdf (how Dedicated would sit in your VPC), soc2-evidence-checklist.pdf

Thanks — I’ll loop Markus for the sizing confirmation and Camila for isolation/runbook details.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Lisa Park <lisa@perceptahealth.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity for Percepta Health — isolation, scaling, SLA

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

Clarifications
- Nightly scoring: the 1.2M docs number is correct but it's likely to grow ~20%/q as more pipelines onboard.
- Latency SLO: 150ms p95 is aggressive on mono-GPU models; we can target it for the shorter path but will need the PoC to validate with realistic loads.
- Isolation: we need both logical tenant isolation and the option for a single-tenant VPC for Phase 2 if data classification requires it.
- Audit logs: must be exportable to our SIEM in realtime (prefer Kafka / S3 exporters).

Requests
- Please attach an example runbook for a canary rollout and automated fallback policy so our SREs can review.
- Can you call out cost delta between "reserved 4 + burst" vs a baseline 6-guaranteed pool? We need ballpark TCO for procurement.

We prefer the PoC week of Jul 6 (the team is stretched on Jun 29). Procurement wants the draft term sheet before the PoC kickoff.

Thanks — I’ll ask procurement to confirm budget banding this week.

Best,
Lisa
Senior Product Ops, Percepta Health

Subject: Re: Qualification: Dedicated GPU capacity for Percepta Health — isolation, scaling, SLA

Thanks Lisa — all good notes. Quick responses inline below and a couple asks for our internal ops/eng alignment: 

- Growth projection: +20%/q noted — that nudges our recommendation to start with 5 reserved GPUs with a burst to 7 (we’ll model cost below).
- Latency validation: agree, PoC must include a synthetic traffic generator with mixed-sequence length profiles. Markus, can you confirm the test harness and the model variants we should run?
- Single-tenant VPC: Camila, can you confirm whether our private deployment template can be contracted for Phase 2 and what minimum term you’d expect?
- Audit exports: we support Kafka/S3 export; I’ll attach the runbook snippet and an example Kafka connector config.

Preliminary TCO notes (rough):
- Config A (5 reserved + burst to 7): ~15% lower monthly cost vs baseline 7-guaranteed, with slightly more complexity in burst handling.
- Config B (7-guaranteed): simpler procurement and a flatter monthly cost profile (preferred by procurement teams).

Next steps (updated)
1) I’ll update the attached workbook with +20% growth and two sizing options (Config A/B) and send by EOD PDT.
2) Markus to outline PoC test harness and models (we aim to replicate daytime assist pattern + nightly scoring).
3) Camila to confirm Private/Single-tenant term assumptions and window for onboarding.
4) Percepta procurement to share desired contract cadence and PO process so we tailor the term sheet.

Markus / Camila — loop in any devops runbook items I missed.

—
Jordan
